the `SecretStore` reads Key Vault **at runtime**, so the next test/run picks it up
immediately (verified 2026-07-25). That is the opposite of secret-injected **env vars**,

**own** `conn-<name>` Key Vault secret, so *one credential shared by N connections exists as N
independent copies*. Renewing the PAT in Snowflake — or writing it under one connection —
leaves the others dead, and **nothing in the product shows the divergence** (#954: datasource
connections have no health signal; #839 gave one only to *orchestration* connections). These

secret they read. **On any credential rotation, write ALL `conn-*` secrets that share it, then
prove it with `POST /connections/{id}/test` per connection** — the connections list will look
identical whether they are alive or dead.

the `SecretStore` reads Key Vault **at runtime**, so the next test/run picks it up
immediately (verified 2026-07-25). That is the opposite of secret-injected **env vars**,
which are a start-time snapshot and do require restarting every dependent revision — see
[[dev-aca-secret-restart-after-pg-recreate]]. Don't generalize one to the other.

unexpected_percent correctness (checked against independently-computed ground truth), and
sample-failure extraction. Also proves the compound_columns_to_be_unique uppercase-column
reflection-casing fix is load-bearing (raw GX call without the fold KeyErrors; our runner,
which folds, succeeds).
"""

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ")
os.environ["UC_SQL_PUSHDOWN"] = "true"

from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckSpec
from backend.app.datasources.unity_catalog import UnityCatalogConfig, UnityCatalogCheckRunner

token = os.environ["DBX_TOKEN"]
config = UnityCatalogConfig.model_validate(
    {
        "warehouse_id": "b6403b6e3734f0ce",
        "workspace_url": "https://dbc-4492dde4-090c.cloud.databricks.com",
    }
)
runner = UnityCatalogCheckRunner(config=config, token=token, catalog="dataq_retail")


def show(label, outcome):
    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")
    for c in outcome.checks:
        print(
            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "
            f"observed={c.observed_value} sample_failures={c.sample_failures}"
        )


# ── Group A: reference.locations (8 rows) ──
show(
    "locations",
    runner.run_checks(
        table="locations",
        schema="reference",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b",
                {"column_A": "close_hour", "column_B": "open_hour"},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal",
                {"column_list": ["open_hour", "close_hour"], "sum_total": 30},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record",
                {"column_list": ["open_hour", "close_hour"]},
            ),
        ],
    ),
)

        checks=[

real dataq_retail tables. Proves: routing (SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES), payload shape,
unexpected_percent correctness (checked against independently-computed ground truth), and
sample-failure extraction. Also proves the compound_columns_to_be_unique uppercase-column
reflection-casing fix is load-bearing (raw GX call without the fold KeyErrors; our runner,
which folds, succeeds).

    UnityCatalogCheckRunner,
    UnityCatalogConfig,
)

token = os.environ["DBX_TOKEN"]

    {
        "warehouse_id": "b6403b6e3734f0ce",
        "workspace_url": "https://dbc-4492dde4-090c.cloud.databricks.com",
    }
)
runner = UnityCatalogCheckRunner(config=config, token=token, catalog="dataq_retail")


def show(label, outcome):
    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")
    for c in outcome.checks:
        print(
            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "
            f"observed={c.observed_value} sample_failures={c.sample_failures}"

)

    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")

            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "

## 2026-08-28/29 — #1624 UC pushdown live verification: Databricks Free Edition workspace was inactivity-deactivated
- The `dataq_retail` warehouse (`b6403b6e3734f0ce`) start call 400'd with `resource-gatekeeper` / `denyReason: INACTIVE` — the Free Edition workspace itself had been auto-deactivated for inactivity. The PAT still authenticated fine (200 on warehouse-info); this is a workspace-level state, not a credential or warehouse-cold-start issue, and **no API/CLI clears it** — only a human browser login to the workspace does. User logged in; warehouse then started normally via `POST /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/{id}/start`.
- With the warehouse up, live-verified all 14 #1624 pushdown types via the real `UnityCatalogCheckRunner.run_checks` against `dataq_retail.reference.{locations,channels,categories,date_dim}` — every `unexpected_percent` matched an independently-computed ground-truth SQL query (e.g. `date_dim` fiscal_week≠fiscal_quarter: 535/539 = 99.2579%, exact match). Also proved the `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` uppercase-column reflection-casing fold is load-bearing on Databricks: an unfolded uppercase `column_list` KeyErrors (`error_message: "'CATEGORY_ID'"`); the runner's fold (mirroring `DatabricksDialect.normalize_name`, same shape as #1616's Snowflake fix) resolves it cleanly.
- Warehouse stopped afterward (`POST .../stop`, 200) to restore the pre-session state; no credential was touched.
- **Lesson for next time:** a Databricks Free Edition workspace can go inactive independently of the Azure harness (`harness_window.sh` doesn't touch it) — if a warehouse `/start` 400s with `DENY_NEW_AND_EXISTING_RESOURCES`/`INACTIVE`, the fix is a browser login, not a retry loop or a warehouse-config check.

- **`backend/app/datasources/unity_catalog.py:448`** — `checks = _fold_reflection_keyed_columns(checks)` was inserted *before* the `try:` at line 457, i.e. outside the `except Exception` block (515-519) that exists specifically to turn a SQL-batch-setup failure into a per-check `errored` `SuiteOutcome` instead of an unhandled crash. `run_checks` (328-380) has no try/except of its own around `_run_sql_checks`, so if the fold call ever raises, the exception propagates past `run_checks` entirely — discarding the dataframe-group results already computed in `by_position` for a mixed suite, turning a partial success into a total run failure. In practice `_reflection_key`'s only real crash risk (non-`str` input to `DatabricksDialect().normalize_name`, e.g. `int`) is already guarded by `isinstance(c, str)` in `fold_reflection_keyed_columns`, and `normalize_name` was empirically robust on real strings (empty, unicode, quotes, 300-char) — so likelihood is low today, but the isolation contract the rest of the method establishes is broken by this one line, and it's calling into third-party dialect internals whose behavior isn't guaranteed across `databricks-sqlalchemy` versions.
- No other off-by-one/wrong-condition/wrong-variable defects found in the touched hunks; `checks[i]`/`by_position` indexing, `clash_set`/`keep` list-comp indices, and `SuiteOutcome` assembly all remain correctly aligned after the fold (fold is a 1:1, order-preserving map — verified by reading `fold_reflection_keyed_columns` in `sql.py:102-125`).

### Angle 2 — Removed-behavior audit
- Snowflake's inline `_fold_reflection_keyed_columns` body was moved verbatim into the shared `fold_reflection_keyed_columns(checks, reflection_keyed_types=..., normalize_name=...)` — compared field-by-field, the new version is behavior-identical (same guard, same `{**spec.kwargs, ...}` copy, same fall-through for non-matching specs, same non-mutation of the input `CheckSpec`/its dict). - The rewritten `test_pushdown_allowlist_partitions_the_catalog` preserves both prior overlap invariants (`SQL_PUSHDOWN ∩ DATAFRAME_ONLY == ∅`, `SQL_PUSHDOWN ∩ frame_only == ∅`) and correctly accounts for the newly-pushed-down `expect_column_pair_values_to_be_in_set` (an `ALLOWLIST_ONLY_TYPES` member, absent from the catalog fixture) via the new `routed - ALLOWLIST_ONLY_TYPES` subtraction. No invariant lost.

### Angle 3 — Cross-file tracer
- Grepped all callers of `fold_reflection_keyed_columns`, `_fold_reflection_keyed_columns` (both files), and `SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES` — only the expected sites (`snowflake.py:219`, `unity_catalog.py:448`, the two test files, `uc_sql_pushdown`/`run_checks`). No stale caller of an old signature, no circular import (`sql.py` importing `CheckSpec` from `base.py` is safe — `base.py` has zero intra-`datasources` imports).

### Angle 4 — Reuse
- **Minor DRY debt**: the *outer* fold loop is now shared, but the per-dialect trio (`_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES = frozenset({...})`, `_reflection_key()` importing a dialect class and calling `.normalize_name(name) or name`, and the one-line `_fold_reflection_keyed_columns` wrapper) is still duplicated near-verbatim in both `snowflake.py:125-143` and `unity_catalog.py:157-171`. A `make_reflection_folder(dialect_cls, types)` factory in `sql.py` would collapse both to one line each. Low value today (only 2 call sites), but ADR 0036 says a third connection-anchored engine is coming, so this pattern will likely be copy-pasted a third time.
- No other module needed/missed the shared helper (grep confirms `iceberg.py`/`flatfile.py` have no analogous reflection-case issue, consistent with them not going through SQLAlchemy table reflection the same way).

### Angle 5 — Simplification
- Nothing beyond angle 4's dedup opportunity. The shared function's signature (`reflection_keyed_types`, `normalize_name` as injected callback) is appropriately generic — no unnecessary abstraction.

### Angle 6 — Efficiency (directly investigated as asked)
- `_reflection_key` is called **once per `str` column, per matching check**, inside the list comprehension in `fold_reflection_keyed_columns` (not once per fold-run, not once per check-list) — so `DatabricksDialect()` gets constructed len(`column_list`) times per `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` check. Benchmarked directly: **~1.2 microseconds per `DatabricksDialect()` construction** (1000 instances in 1.26ms). Even a suite with dozens of compound-unique checks over wide column lists would add single-digit milliseconds at most — **verified negligible, not a real cost**, despite looking wasteful on read. (Note: this pattern is pre-existing for Snowflake, not introduced by this PR — the PR just replicates it for UC.)

### Angle 7 — Altitude
- **`_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` is scoped to only `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique`**, but two *other* newly-pushed-down types — `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal` and `expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record` — also take a `column_list` kwarg with the exact same shape. I traced GX's actual provider code to check whether they need the same fold: both route through the generic `multicolumn_function_partial`/`multicolumn_condition_partial` machinery, which calls `get_dbms_compatible_metric_domain_kwargs` (in `great_expectations/expectations/metrics/util.py`) to case-normalize `column_list` against the real reflected columns *before* building `sa.column(...)` references — and, unlike `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique`'s bespoke `_sqlalchemy_function`, they never do a raw `.c[name]` dict lookup against a reflected `Table`/`Select.c` collection (the actual KeyError site for #1616). So on the current GX version (1.17.2, matching `environment.yml`'s pin) these two likely do **not** need `_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` membership. This is a defensible narrow scoping, not obviously a bug — but it's exactly the kind of bandaid the PR's own docs warn about re-discovering: nothing records *why* these two lookalike types were excluded, so a future contributor (or the #1624 conversion of the remaining legacy frame types) has to redo this GX-internals trace from scratch to confirm it's still safe. Worth a one-line comment next to `_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` explaining the distinction (bespoke `.c[name]` join vs. generic `sa.column()` build), and/or a live-Databricks regression test with an all-caps `column_list` against `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal` to close the loop the same way #1616 did for compound-unique.

### Angle 8 — Conventions (CLAUDE.md)
- No version-pin violations (no new deps), no credentials, no migration involved, no ADF/Airflow-as-datasource violation. The two changes (extract shared helper + expand pushdown set) are causally coupled (the extraction exists *because* `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` — which needs the fold — is one of the 14 newly-pushed types), so this reads as one functionality, not a "batch unrelated changes" violation.

---

### Flat list — strongest candidates

1. **`backend/app/datasources/unity_catalog.py:448`** — `_fold_reflection_keyed_columns(checks)` runs *before* the method's `try:` (line 457), outside the exception boundary that exists to convert SQL-batch-setup failures into isolated per-check `errored` outcomes. *Failure scenario:* any exception from the fold step (third-party dialect quirk, future `databricks-sqlalchemy` behavior change) propagates uncaught through `run_checks`, discarding already-computed dataframe-group results for the whole suite instead of failing just the SQL group.

2. **`backend/app/datasources/unity_catalog.py:159` / `snowflake.py:131`** (Altitude) — `_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` includes only `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique`, but `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal` and `expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record` (both newly pushed down, both take `column_list`) are not covered and the scoping rationale isn't recorded anywhere in code. *Cost:* my trace of GX's provider code suggests these two are safe (they don't do the `.c[name]` reflected-dict lookup that causes #1616), but nothing stops the next engineer from having to re-derive that from scratch, and it wasn't live-verified with a mismatched-case `column_list` the way compound-unique was for #1616.

3. **`backend/app/datasources/unity_catalog.py:162-165` / `snowflake.py:134-137`** (Reuse) — the per-dialect trio (`_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES`, `_reflection_key`, the wrapper) is duplicated near-identically across both files; only the inner fold-loop was shared. *Cost:* a third connection-anchored engine (ADR 0036 — DMF/DQX/Dataplex) needing the same pattern means a third copy-paste instead of one factory call.

4. **`fold_reflection_keyed_columns` → `_reflection_key`** (Efficiency, angle 6) — `DatabricksDialect()`/`SnowflakeDialect()` is constructed once per column string rather than hoisted once per fold-run. *Verified benign*: ~1.2µs/construction, negligible even at scale — reporting this as a checked-and-cleared item rather than a real cost, since the task specifically asked for the investigation.

5. **Test coverage gap** (Angle 2/pr-test-analyzer territory) — no test exercises `_run_sql_checks` actually invoking `_fold_reflection_keyed_columns` end-to-end (only the pure function is unit-tested in isolation). This mirrors the pre-existing Snowflake test pattern, so it's low-priority, but it means finding #1 above (fold outside the try/except) has no regression test that would catch it if `_reflection_key` ever does raise.

No other correctness bugs, removed-behavior regressions, or reuse misses were found beyond what's listed above and the already-known column/column_A/column_B/column_list clash-detection gap you're separately verifying.</result>

Benchmarked directly: **~1.2 microseconds per `DatabricksDialect()` construction** (1000 instances in 1.26ms). Even a suite with dozens of compound-unique checks over wide column lists would add single-digit milliseconds at most — **verified negligible, not a real cost**, despite looking wasteful on read. (Note: this pattern is pre-existing for Snowflake, not introduced by this PR — the PR just replicates it for UC.)

### Angle 7 — Altitude
- **`_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` is scoped to only `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique`**, but two *other* newly-pushed-down types — `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal` and `expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record` — also take a `column_list` kwarg with the exact same shape. So on the current GX version (1.17.2, matching `environment.yml`'s pin) these two likely do **not** need `_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` membership. ### Angle 8 — Conventions (CLAUDE.md)
- No version-pin violations (no new deps), no credentials, no migration involved, no ADF/Airflow-as-datasource violation. The two changes (extract shared helper + expand pushdown set) are causally coupled (the extraction exists *because* `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` — which needs the fold — is one of the 14 newly-pushed types), so this reads as one functionality, not a "batch unrelated changes" violation.

2. **`backend/app/datasources/unity_catalog.py:159` / `snowflake.py:131`** (Altitude) — `_REFLECTION_KEYED_TYPES` includes only `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique`, but `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal` and `expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record` (both newly pushed down, both take `column_list`) are not covered and the scoping rationale isn't recorded anywhere in code. *Cost:* my trace of GX's provider code suggests these two are safe (they don't do the `.c[name]` reflected-dict lookup that causes #1616), but nothing stops the next engineer from having to re-derive that from scratch, and it wasn't live-verified with a mismatched-case `column_list` the way compound-unique was for #1616.

def test_pushdown_default_is_on() -> None:
    # The test suite pins UC_SQL_PUSHDOWN=false in conftest; the SHIPPED default is on.
    from backend.app.core.config import Settings

    assert Settings.model_fields["uc_sql_pushdown"].default is True


def test_index_column_clash_is_case_insensitive(
    tmp_path: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Databricks resolves identifiers case-insensitively; the clash compare must too."""
    from backend.app.datasources import unity_catalog as uc_module
    from backend.app.datasources.gx_runner import run_expectations as real

    seen: list[Any] = []

    def _spy(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        seen.append(kwargs.get("index_columns"))
        return real(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(uc_module, "run_expectations", _spy)
    _pushdown_on(monkeypatch)
    runner = _uc_runner()
    _orders_sql_seam(runner, tmp_path, monkeypatch, rows=[(1, 10)])
    runner.run_checks(
        table="orders",
        schema="sales",
        checks=[CheckSpec("expect_column_values_to_not_be_null", {"column": "ID"})],
        index_columns=["id"],
    )
    assert seen == [None]

def test_index_column_clash_is_detected_via_column_a_and_column_b(
    tmp_path: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """A pair check keyed on column_A/column_B, not `column`, still drops the
    index request when either side is the index column."""
    from backend.app.datasources import unity_catalog as uc_module
    from backend.app.datasources.gx_runner import run_expectations as real

    seen: list[Any] = []

    def _spy(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        seen.append(kwargs.get("index_columns"))
        return real(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(uc_module, "run_expectations", _spy)
    _pushdown_on(monkeypatch)
    runner = _uc_runner()
    _orders_sql_seam(runner, tmp_path, monkeypatch, rows=[(1, 10)])
    runner.run_checks(
        table="orders",
        schema="sales",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b",
                {"column_A": "amt", "column_B": "id"},
            )
        ],
        index_columns=["id"],
    )
    assert seen == [None]

    """A check keyed on column_list, not `column`, still drops the index request

    from backend.app.datasources import unity_catalog as uc_module

        seen.append(kwargs.get("index_columns"))

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fixup: fix SQL-pushdown index-column clash detection for the new types

/code-review caught: the Databricks index-column clash workaround only checked the
`column` kwarg, so the newly pushed-down column_A/column_B/column_list-keyed types
(pair checks, multicolumn_sum_to_equal, select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record,
compound_columns_to_be_unique) were never routed away from a colliding index request,
reproducing the duplicate-field-name Databricks error the clash code exists to avoid.
Generalized to a _spec_columns() helper covering all three kwarg shapes.

Also moved the reflection-casing fold inside the SQL group's own try/except so a
failure there is an isolated errored outcome rather than an unhandled crash, and
live-verified that the two other column_list-keyed types (multicolumn_sum_to_equal,
select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record) don't need the same fold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -25
